title: Netskope Admin Audit Trail

description: Administrative changes to Netskope policies, steering configs, and tenant settings have global impact. Audit trail ensures accountability and change correlation.
value: Security governance teams audit all Netskope administrative changes — policy modifications, protection disables, admin account additions — flagging out-of-hours changes and high-impact deletions that can create instant organization-wide security gaps.
implementation: Alert on after-hours policy changes or bulk rule modifications. Correlate admin changes with enforcement anomalies in UC-17.3.37. Require change tickets for policy modifications.
visualization: Table (recent changes), Timeline (admin activity), Bar chart (changes by admin).

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Netskope admin audit events in `index=netskope` with `sourcetype=netskope:audit` or from the Netskope REST API audit endpoint. Key fields: `admin_user`, `event` (Create/Update/Delete/Login), `object_type` (Policy/Profile/Publisher/Configuration), `object_name`, `details`, `timestamp`.
• Netskope admin changes can have immediate, organization-wide impact. A misconfigured DLP policy, disabled threat protection, or removed CASB rule can create an instant security gap.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Verify admin audit events:
```spl
index=netskope sourcetype="netskope:audit" earliest=-30d
| stats count by event, object_type
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Admin change log:
```spl
index=netskope sourcetype="netskope:audit" earliest=-7d
| eval change_hour=strftime(_time, "%H")
| eval out_of_hours=if(change_hour<"08" OR change_hour>"18", "YES", "no")
| table _time, admin_user, event, object_type, object_name, details, out_of_hours
| sort - _time
```

Understanding this SPL: Lists all admin changes with out-of-hours flagging. Critical changes: deleting a real-time protection policy, disabling threat protection, modifying DLP rules, or adding admin users. Out-of-hours changes bypass the normal review process and are higher risk.

High-impact changes:
```spl
index=netskope sourcetype="netskope:audit" earliest=-7d
| where event=="Delete" OR match(object_type, "(?i)policy|protection|dlp")
| stats count by admin_user, event, object_type
| sort - count
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) Make a test change in Netskope Admin. Verify the audit event.
(b) In Netskope: Settings > Administration > Audit Log. Compare.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — Admin changes per day. Row 2 — High-impact changes. Row 3 — Out-of-hours changes.
Alert: Immediate on policy deletion or threat protection disable.

Runbook:
1. **Policy deletion** — Verify with admin. Roll back if unintended.
2. **Threat protection disabled** — Critical. Re-enable immediately.
3. **New admin added** — Verify authorization with security team.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **No audit events** — Audit logging may require a separate API endpoint. Check Netskope REST API v2.
• **`details` empty** — Some admin actions don't include change details in the audit.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Netskope Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 3808)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=netskope:audit into casb. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`admin_user, object_type`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Every change an administrator makes to our cloud security settings is recorded. We pay special attention to dangerous changes like disabling security features or deleting rules, especially when they happen outside normal hours, because one wrong change can leave the entire organization unprotected.
